authorityRule: A source establishes only the claim it actually supports. Product labeling is not organizational endorsement; a possible experience is not authorized capability; retail presence is not publisher authority.

claims.claim: Baker Targets is a side project of The Baker Press, Inc., an Orlando printing company in business since 1968.
Baker identifies its own pressmen, graphic artists, custom-target workflow, and Orlando printing operation; in-house design and printing are confirmed for the described operation.

A six-page publisher-authored Game Target Instructions PDF defines bounded rules for six products: Arcade (GF-Arc), Battleship (GF-Battleship), Dartboard (GF-DB; two games), Pinball (GF-Pinball), Candyville (GF-Candyville), and Primary (GF-Primary).

ruleSummary.GF-Arc: Thirteen-shot multiplayer point accumulation with explicit region values, miss penalty, and highest-total winner.
ruleSummary.GF-Battleship: Two-player opponent-board ship collection with declared bonus-circle attempts, replacement hits, whole-ship effect, and lost-turn penalty.
ruleSummary.GF-DB: A declared-number points game with double/triple rings and bullseye finale, plus an ordered 1-through-20 progression game.
ruleSummary.GF-Pinball: Two-round points, extra-shot, bonus-shot, and final Collect Man win state.
ruleSummary.GF-Candyville: Color-owned ordered path traversal with turns, opponent-color benefit, slide branches, color reassignment, and reset-to-start penalty.
ruleSummary.GF-Primary: Multi-player memory/repetition sequence with optional caller and color, number, or combined cue modes.

claims.capabilityImpact: Closes the public publisher-rules evidence gap for these six product experiences. It does not activate any capability until exact profile, UGO, registration, and governance validation are approved.

claims.claim: Candyville supplies the first direct publisher-rule evidence in the seven-publisher corpus for ordered path traversal with branching slides, mutable player color, and reset-to-start state.
claims.capabilityImpact: Genuine new behavior-family candidate: publisher-defined path traversal. Gear 6 explicitly excluded path behavior, so this cannot be silently assigned to collection/hand or activated without a Founder specification.

claims.claim: Baker says its B29 Florida G target is used for the Florida G firearms license and references a page in a Florida manual; this establishes publisher product intent, not the current government course or an official relationship.
claims.capabilityImpact: Qualification remains authority-gated pending the applicable government course profile and official-claim authorities.

Birchwood Casey states that its shooting and gun-care business dates to 1948 and provides direct ecommerce and customer contact.

No authoritative NRA, GSSF, USPSA, IDPA, CMP, military, or law-enforcement organizational relationship was established. A customer review mentioning NRA B-8 scoring is not publisher or NRA authority.

EZ Aim is a target brand/family sold by The Allen Company; Allen Company, Inc. publishes its Louisville, Colorado address and direct contact paths.
Allen says the company began more than 50 years ago in Broomfield, Colorado, and designs/tests outdoor products with outdoor experts.

Allen explicitly identifies NSSF and other associations, conservation partners, and separately identifies officially licensed brand partnerships including Ruger and Girls With Guns; these claim types are preserved separately.
The page mentions an individual partner's NRA instructor credential; it does not establish an Allen/EZ Aim relationship with NRA or NRA authority for EZ Aim targets.
An Allen catalog labels specific EZ Aim paper products 'Made in USA with domestic and imported components'; the status is product scoped and not generalized to the company catalog.
Academy currently carries EZ Aim branded target offerings; this is observed retailer availability only.
Allen links official Facebook, YouTube, Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Pinterest, and Instagram channels from its publisher site.

The current Allen homepage promotes an EZ Aim Sasquatch target not present by name in the preserved August 20 EZ Aim normalized corpus; this is a catalog-change candidate, not an ingested product record.
